title: Lien Process Standard for Self-Storage Unit Rental Agreements
content:
## 1. Anchor and counting
The lien process on a Self-Storage Unit Rental Agreement runs from the delinquency date, the due date of the oldest unpaid billing period of the delinquency cycle (the delinquency anchor date), and every step is dated in calendar days. Day counts start the day after the anchor date and the step is allowed on the day the count is reached. The day counts and fees are the class's figures.

## 2. Steps and their earliest dates
2.1 **Company overlock.** The company overlock may be applied when the handling date is not earlier than the delinquency anchor date plus the class's overlock day count. The overlock posts the class's overlock fee.
2.2 **Preliminary lien letter.** The preliminary lien letter is sent by first-class mail and email at the class's preliminary-letter day count.
2.3 **Formal lien notice.** The formal lien notice may be sent when the handling date is not earlier than the delinquency anchor date plus the class's lien-notice day count, by certified mail and email, and it moves the rental to lien noticed. It posts the class's lien notice fee.
2.4 **Sale advertisement.** The sale may be advertised when the handling date is not earlier than the lien notice date plus the class's advertisement day count; the advertisement sets a scheduled sale date at least the class's minimum days after the advertisement date and moves the rental to auction scheduled. It posts the class's advertisement fee.
2.5 **Lock cut for inventory.** The tenant lock may be cut for inventory on or after the advertisement date. It posts the class's lock cut fee.
2.6 **Lien sale.** The lien sale may be held when the handling date is not earlier than the advertisement date plus the class's minimum days from advertisement to sale.

Each fee in 2.1, 2.3, 2.4 and 2.5 is posted against the delinquency cycle's anchor date.

## 3. Status and repetition
Lien steps are taken only while the rental is in delinquent, lien noticed or auction scheduled status. Each step is taken once per delinquency cycle. The overlock is removed with an overlock-removed step when the rental is redeemed.

## 4. Lien holds
No lien notice, advertisement, lock cut or sale may proceed while a lien hold is in place. A lien hold is placed when the tenant or a family member reports active-duty military service backed by orders on file, or when the tenant reports a bankruptcy filing with a case number, and it stays until a lien-hold-released step is recorded. Rent and late fees keep accruing during a hold. The hold rests on the tenant's report together with what the records hold — the orders on file or the case number given — and on the agreement's lien steps.

## Boundary illustration (hypothetical class with a 10-day overlock count and 35-day lien-notice count)
Oldest unpaid period due 1 March:

| Handling date | Day after anchor | Overlock allowed | Lien notice allowed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10 March | 9 | no | no |
| 11 March | 10 | yes | no |
| 4 April | 34 | yes | no |
| 5 April | 35 | yes | yes |

A lien notice sent on 5 April in a class with a 15-day advertisement count allows the advertisement from 20 April; with a 10-day minimum, a sale advertised on 20 April may be held from 30 April, and its scheduled sale date is 30 April or later.

## Hold matrix

| Step | Proceeds while a hold is in place |
|---|---|
| lien notice, advertisement, lock cut, sale | no |
| rent and late fees | keep accruing |
